title: Browser HOST_TIME emits malformed fractional-hour offsets
description:
`indigo_server/resource/indigo.js:493-509` divides timezone minutes by60 and concatenates `'00'`, instead of formatting separate whole hours and remainder minutes. With getTimezoneOffset()=-330 the actual committed function produces suffix `+05.500`, whereas an ISO numeric UTC+05:30 offset is `+0530` (or `+05:30`). Every authored page calls timestamp() for initially empty Server.HOST_TIME; server setter `indigo_server.c:1540-1550` forwards the value to its existing date-management helper. Fractional-hour locales can fail first-time host clock setup. Remediation: format signed absolute hours and minutes separately, or use a validated UTC repre Full evidence: C-04. Remediation: format signed absolute hours and minutes separately, or use a validated UTC representation supported by the helper; regress ±30/45-minute offsets and ordinary whole-hour timezones. The test replaced only Date.getTimezoneOffset in an isolated VM; no system clock was changed.
